statement.p: Find the volume between the cone x = \sqrt{y^2 + z^2} and the sphere x^2+y^2+z^2=16.

static.solution:
x-axis and intersects the sphere in the circle (y^2 + z^2) + y^2 + z^2 = 16, or y^2 + z^2 = 8
We use spherical coordinates with \phi measured from the x-axis and \theta measured in the yz-plane. The cone is given by \phi = \pi/4. The sphere has equation \rho =4. Thus \mbox{Vol } = \int_0^{2\pi} \int_0^{\pi/4}\int_0^{4} \rho^2\sin\phi\,d\rho\,d\phi\,d\theta, so \mbox{Vol } = \int_0^{2\pi} \int_0^{\pi/4} \frac{\rho^3}3 \sin\phi\Bigg|_0^{4} d\phi\,d\theta = \int_0^{2\pi} \int_0^{\pi/4} \frac{64}{3}\sin\phi\,d\phi\,d\theta = \int_0^{2\pi} -\frac{64}{3}\cos\phi\Bigg|_0^{\pi/4} d\theta = \int_0^{2\pi} \frac{64}{3}\left(1-\frac1{\sqrt{2}}\right)\,d\theta = \frac{128}{3}\pi\left(1-\frac1{\sqrt{2}}\right).
